title: Gaze_characteristics_of_elite_and_near_e
universal_lens: The visual search process is modeled as a non-stationary stochastic point process. Elite performers minimize the Kullback-Leibler divergence between their fixation sequence and the optimal information-gathering path, utilizing rapid early sampling to reduce environmental entropy before committing to a terminal state.
gsi_mapping: GSI maps gaze duration to Bayesian posterior updates over tactical states. Early rapid fixations act as high-frequency priors, while the final prolonged fixation (F/T-1) represents a conformal prediction interval collapse, ensuring the selected defensive action maintains robust coverage against dynamic opponent trajectories.
gse_mapping: GSE treats the open-skill environment as a continuous Markov Decision Process. The 'Quiet Eye' phase acts as a temporal gating mechanism, freezing state transitions until the sensory buffer reaches a sufficient confidence threshold to trigger the discrete motor execution policy.

primitives.name: Early Rapid Sampling Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: First, fixation/ tracking (F/T) gaze early in the trial were significantly shorter than the final F/T and confirmed that the elite group fixated the tactical locations more rapidly than the non-elite on successful plays.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: \Delta t_{early}: early fixation duration (s), \lambda: spatial sampling rate (fixations/s)
primitives.assumptions: Information gain per unit time is maximized by minimizing dwell time during broad environmental scanning.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity occurs if \Delta t_{early} drops below the minimum neural integration window (~50ms).

primitives.assumptions: A sustained final fixation is required to bind perceptual features into a unified motor program.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Motor initiation fails if \tau_{QE} is interrupted by external perturbations or internal hesitation.
